title: toolcall-metadata-normalizer-and-choice-semantics
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: users integrating external tools via the OpenAI-style function/tool calling surface were seeing divergent behavior between streaming partial tool suggestions and final tool_choice selection. This caused heuristic mismatches across clients and made fallbacks brittle. This PR standardizes how tool metadata is normalized, how tool_choice semantics are computed, and how partial tool messages are framed in streams so that downstream adapters (OpenAI-compat SDKs and third-party plugins) can deterministically interpret both suggestions and final selections. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a lightweight ToolMetadataNormalizer that maps incoming external tool schemas (arbitrary keys, nested param shapes) into a stable internal shape (name, id, canonical_schema_hash, user_facing_descriptor). 2) Change tool_choice semantics: tool_choice now represents a single deterministic selection token that includes selection_reason and confidence_score fields, and RFC-style backward-compatible aliases are emitted for older clients. 3) Streaming partials: add explicit event type "tool_suggest" for early streaming hints and ensure they contain canonical_schema_hash and a partial_descriptor to avoid ambiguous partial tool fragments. 4) Normalizer registry: runtime maintains a pluggable mapping registry so new tool schema versions can be onboarded without runtime restarts. 5) SDK and compat layers: update the OpenAI-compat adapter to translate function call shapes into the normalizer input and expose the canonical fields in the tool invocation envelope. 6) Tests and canary rollout hooks plus a migration guide. Backwards compatibility and migration: the adapter emits both v1-style function_call fields and the new tool_schema_v2 envelope when a client advertises openai_compat:v2. If client only supports v1, the system falls back to the legacy function_call name/index semantics plus a stable "tool_alias" header that maps to canonical id. The migration guide describes how to opt-in, how to validate via the canary flag, and how to read the selection_reason and confidence_score for monitoring. Rollout plan: unit and integration tests ran in CI, then 1% canary on dedicated clusters for 48 hours, followed by gradual ramp to 50% and full by 7 days pending no regressions. Related: design doc https://go/redwood/design/tool-normalizer and Linear ENG-8721. Checklist: [x] design doc linked  [x] unit tests added  [x] integration tests added  [x] compat adapter updates  [x] docs and migration guide updated  [x] canary configuration added

review_comments: Ravi Patel: Can we avoid adding latency to cold-paths? Suggest caching normalized entries keyed by schema hash.  Author reply: Added registry-based LRU cache in normalizer_registry and benchmarked cold-path impact (<2ms).

Elena Gomez: The selection_reason field is great for observability, but please ensure it's small and enum-like to avoid token bloat.  Author reply: selection_reason is an enum (route, score, user_hint, fallback) in the serialized token. Tests updated.

Marta Chen: Need an explicit compatibility test for clients that only speak v1.  Author reply: added tests/integration/test_tool_choice_streaming.py to assert dual-envelope behavior and legacy alias header presence.

release_notes: Normalize external tool schemas and standardize tool_choice semantics. Adds tool_suggest streaming hint events and a normalizer registry. Backward-compatible with OpenAI-style function_call v1 via dual-envelope emission. See docs/compat/tool_schema_migration.md for migration steps.
